svg.aria-label: The experiment protocol: a shared healthy window, cross-fitted thresholds, and both arms indistinguishable to the detector
svg.text: The split, and what each arm spends it on
Both arms consume the SAME healthy stretch. The residual arm spends part of it on a regime model; the raw arm has none.
true onset
HEALTHY

fit

false alarms counted before the onset; detection measured after it
Residual arm
[0, fit) regime model and residual model
[fit, calib) detector baseline
Total healthy consumed: the whole window.
Raw arm
[0, calib) detector baseline, all of it
no regime model to spend anything on
Total healthy consumed: the same window.
Until an adversarial review, this arm got only [fit, calib).
And four rules that make the comparison mean something
1. Both arms reach the detector as the SAME kind of object, so it cannot tell them apart.
2. Matched false-alarm BUDGET, not a matched threshold value: a z-scored residual and a channel in bar are different scales.
3. Alarms are EVENTS, not samples. An hour above the line is one alarm an operator answers, not sixty.
4. The bootstrap resamples UNITS. Consecutive cycles of one machine are not independent observations.
Thresholds are cross-fitted across units, so no threshold is chosen on the record it scores.
Channel selection reads the baseline window only, never the faulty region.
